description: Gripper: new Gen 16 combining Gen 15 + Gen 9 (Jake, by voice). Take inspiration from Gen 9. Rename the current Gen 16 to Gen 17. Make a new Gen 16 that combines Gen 15 and Gen 9, taking the best of both: keep Gen 15's length; keep the ridges but make them shallower, about 1 mm, less pronounced; make it more rounded like Gen 9 (knobs more rounded); have it come to a nice point like Gen 9 does, but the two sides should actually touch at the point; remove the black tip from Gen 15 so it is all yellow. Worker note: use the dual-render workflow (three.js vision render + OpenSCAD STL, same angles, diffed; STL is truth).

results.notes: Looking quite nice. (1) At the large circle toward the end of the fingers there's an indent — smooth it out. (2) The outside profile running in toward the tip should be more of a straight line — it can round slightly, but straighter. (3) Near the tip, the two fingers should never run parallel — they should always converge at less than parallel, so the closed shape reads like a triangle coming to the point. The source of truth is the key reference photo cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png.

results.identified_issue: trace_photo.py: KNOBS swells 13/11 -> 30/28 px, KNOB_SWELL_PX 5->6, new KNOB_BASE_SIGMA (gaussian on the base ramp eased in from both ends so it still joins the trace). WEDGE half_deg 4.5->15, cap 0.40->2.0 (3.0 left a parallel 3 mm slot that stepped back in at the JAW_FOLLOW blend ~25 mm back). WEDGE_R1 kept; KEEP_WIDTH=1 adds (r2 inner - r1 inner) to the outer edge so the beak isn't thinned. NOSE: cubic Bezier over the outer edge's last 7 mm, arriving 65 deg off-axis (90 read as a dome); 6 mm coincided with gripper.scad tip_zone and produced a non-manifold edge. NEEDLE A outer 2.8->4.0. beak_slots now reads slot fractions on the r1 beak (closed_jaw(r1=True)); otherwise two slots broke through (genus 31). gripper.scad: tip_thick 0.5->2.4, half_thick parabola f^2 (ease() removed; concept.js matched). check_geometry: CONTACT_DEG 6->20; target gap read as min over the same +-0.5 mm window as the model (a steep wedge made the window bias read as 0.17 mm error). Pivot unchanged 27.2517. closed_trace.json gap_fit (A d^3.1) is now far below the design; Jake's reading of the photo overrides it. Unverified: print strength, and whether 'thicker tip' meant plan or side view (both were done).
results.summary: Gen 16 edited in place: much rounder bumps, a wide V behind the point, and a thick rounded tip, matched to the closed photo.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 16 is edited in place against the closed photo, which you marked as the key reference.

Bumps: each of the two bump-outs is now about 2.3 times wider and 1.2 mm high. That makes the crest radius about 4 mm instead of 1.4, and the edge under them is smoothed, so they read as soft humps rather than knobs.

V behind the point: closed, only the points touch. Right behind them each inner edge leaves at 15 degrees, a 30 degree V (26 degrees measured 1–2 mm back, was 6.8). The gap grows to 2 mm by about 6 mm back and never narrows again.

Thicker tip: in side view the point is now 2.4 mm thick instead of 0.5, with a fuller taper that stays thick and rounds in at the end. In plan view, the outer edge moves out by as much as the V cuts from the inner edge, so the beak keeps its width. Its last 7 mm rounds inward into the point, like the photo, instead of running straight in to a needle.

All checks pass: watertight, 33 holes, no collisions, and only the last half-millimetre touches. The three.js render and the STL match at 98–100%. previews/compare_closed_photo.png puts the photo next to the closed model. Nothing is printed. The 30 degrees and 2 mm are read by eye from the photo, not measured.

results.notes: Gen 16 looks pretty good, I like a lot of it. Edit Gen 16 in place (v016_generalist_rounded_point; no new gen number). (1) Round the two bump-outs along the length even further - really rounded. (2) Make the tip thicker; it should still come to a single point where the two sides touch. (3) Behind the tip, the two sides should diverge at a sharper angle so they only touch at the tip, not all along the way - the gap opens up rapidly going back from the tip (current V is 6.8 deg; make it much wider).

results.identified_issue:
Interpretation: 'keep the ridges but make them shallower, about 1 mm' — Gen 15's serration grooves are already 0.4 mm deep, so 'shallower to 1 mm' can't mean them; read as the two inner-edge knobs (6 mm step at photo x~637 and a bump at x~680-690). They are now trace_photo.py KNOBS: a hand-drawn spline ramp + two cos^2 swells of KNOB_SWELL_PX=5 px (1 mm) along the outward normal. If Jake meant grooves, change gripper.scad ridge.
Rename: folder v016_generalist_simple -> v017_generalist_simple (text Gen 16 -> Gen 17 only; STLs re-exported because the gallery publisher rejects STLs older than their sources and fell back to one merged mesh, which broke Scripts/test_gripper_poses.py). publish_designs.py ids and poses.js updated. New Gen 16 pivot 27.2517 (echoed from the scad).
Gen 16 = copy of Gen 15 pipeline with: trace contour resample+gaussian SMOOTH_SIGMA=4 (Gen 9) instead of RDP 1.5; PATCHES = Gen 9's blade-root S and J-hook; HIDDEN_HOLES nudged 1.5 px in (smoothed root corner cut its wall to 0.93 mm in trace); gripper.scad tip_thick 1.6->0.5 with Gen 9 ease(); pad removed.
check_geometry gap_profile: cuts at a single z could land in groove bottoms (0.8 mm too wide; phase depends on arc length, which smoothing changed). Now takes innermost reach over +-0.5 mm (one pitch) for d>=3 mm. Gen 15's check is phase-lucky, not changed.
Scripts/check_gripper_closure.py marks Gen 13-16 FAIL because its criterion expects most of the length to touch; these gens are point-only by design (Gen 16 tip gap 0.0 mm).
Dual render: cad/compare/designs.py now discovers <Project>/versions/vNNN_*/web/concept.js (parts from viewer_parts.json, sheet previews/compare_web_stl.png, notes compare_web_stl.md; --export runs the folder's export_models.py). concept.js fetches web/concept.json, which export_models.py writes from gripper.scad part="concept" echo. IoU front 97 / side 100 / top 100 / iso 99 / exploded 99.
Not verified: printability of 0.5 mm point; Jake's visual judgement of knob height.
results.summary: Built a new Gen 16 that combines Gen 15 and Gen 9, and renamed the old Gen 16 to Gen 17.
results.detailed_description:
New Gen 16 keeps Gen 15's length, beak and contact. Closed, only the points touch: 0.0 mm gap at the tip, a 6.8° V behind it. The black tip pad is gone, so each finger is one yellow piece.

From Gen 9 it takes the rounder outline (the whole traced edge is smoothed), the rounded J-hook at the base, a smooth S-curve where the blade starts, and the thin point. In side view the blade now thins to a 0.5 mm point like Gen 9, not Gen 15's 1.6 mm blunt end.

I read "ridges, about 1 mm" as the two square knobs on the inner edge, mid-shank. They're now rounded bumps 1 mm high on a smooth ramp. The fine 0.4 mm serration teeth are unchanged; if you meant those, tell me.

The old Gen 16 (the simple handheld) is Gen 17, unchanged. All checks pass. The three.js vision and the STL render match at 97–100% from every angle. Nothing is printed, and a 0.5 mm point may be fragile.

summary: The Gen 16 gripper has an indent at the large circle near the finger ends, and its outer profile toward the tip is too curved. Smooth the indent, straighten the profile, and keep the fingers always converging near the tip so the closed shape reads as a triangle, matching the closed reference photo.
